scholarships.title: 2026-2027 OAS - Universidad del Desarrollo Scholarship Opportunity (dLab Global)
scholarships.official_source: General Secretariat of the Organization of American States (GS/OAS) and Universidad del Desarrollo
scholarships.official_source_url: https://www.oas.org/en/scholarships/PAEC/2026/2026-2027 OAS - The UDD Scholarship Program Announcement.pdf
scholarships.application_link: https://www.oas.org/en/scholarships/PAEC/2026/2026-2027 OAS - The UDD Scholarship Program Announcement.pdf

existing.description: The GS/OAS and the Universidad del Desarrollo in Chile fund USD 3,400 of the USD 3,800 total course fee for a 4-month online certificate in Global Innovation and Entrepreneurship (dLab Global 2026), focused on SDG 13 climate action. The selected candidate remains responsible for USD 400 of the course fee, plus study materials or equipment, internet access, and any additional fees not included in the offer. Living costs, travel and insurance are not addressed at all in the announcement, so this is not full funding and there is no stipend to live on.
eligibility: Be a citizen or permanent resident of an OAS member state, except Chile.
Have a strong interest in innovation and entrepreneurship.
Innovative resilience building business concepts closely linked to climate or environmental resilience is especially encouraged, or one that addresses a need in the market.
Can 'think outside the box,' exhibit critical thinking skills, and have a quest for discovery or investigative learning.
Demonstrate the ability to lead and inspire others.
Be a young professional who has an idea to develop, or is in the process of developing a small or medium enterprise in an active OAS member state.
Have a strong background in business management.
Be proficient in English.
Commit to at least 4.5 hours a week to the course over a one-semester period consisting of synchronous (live) and asynchronous content.
Have access to a computer with a reliable Internet connection, with appropriate video and audio functions.
Commit to covering the remaining course fee of USD 400 to the UDD.
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be citizens or permanent residents of an active OAS Member State other than Chile, be proficient in English, have a strong business management background, and commit to paying the remaining USD 400 course fee.
benefits: Experts in innovation are invited to speak about their projects during the course.
Connection with the innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem at UDD and in Chile.
coverage: USD 3,400 of the total course fee, contributed jointly by the GS/OAS and the University, out of a total cost of USD 3,800.
Access to the 100% online course delivered through UDD's Canvas platform.
A formal certificate issued by the Universidad del Desarrollo on successful completion of the program.
requirements: Submit a complete application through the online application link, including all supporting documents.
Cover the remaining USD 400 course fee to the UDD.
The scholarship will be formally awarded only after selected recipients sign an OAS Acceptance Form agreeing to its terms and conditions.
Refrain from engaging in activities incompatible with OAS scholarship recipient status, in accordance with the Acceptance Form rules.
Comply with all academic guidelines requested by UDD and submit updates to those guidelines and requirements made by UDD's academic authorities.
documents: Government-issued identification: a copy of either the passport ID page or the national ID card.
Business Concept Statement: a one-paragraph description of an innovative and resilient business concept that addresses an identified problem or market need.

Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Résumé, updated, detailing educational background and professional experience, including relevant professional training, certificates and awards in innovation and entrepreneurship if available.

Proof of English Proficiency (if applicable): an official transcript confirming completion of studies at an English-speaking university or college within the past five years; or TOEFL 570 or higher (paper-based), 230 or higher (computer-based), or 79 or higher (internet-based/IBT); or an IELTS score of 6.5 or equivalent.

Proof of Additional Funds (USD 400): documentation demonstrating the ability to cover the remaining USD 400, which may be one or a combination of a rental agreement, a bank statement or official bank letter, an employer letter confirming salary during study leave with pay, or a letter confirming a student loan, grant, financial aid or additional scholarship.
existing.english_requirement: Applicants whose native language is not English must submit an official transcript confirming completion of studies at an English-speaking university or college within the past five years; or TOEFL 570+ (paper), 230+ (computer), or 79+ (internet-based/IBT); or IELTS 6.5 or equivalent.
application_method: Prepare all supporting documents combined into one single PDF file not exceeding 5 MB, in English or with an official English translation.
Complete the OAS online scholarship application, noting that the system permits only one document upload.
Submit the complete application package with all supporting documents via the OAS link no later than 31 January 2027.
If pre-selected, respond to the email contact and take part in an interview with the scholarship selection committee in English, if necessary.
If finally selected, sign the formal OAS acceptance form after being contacted by email with the scholarship offer and acceptance instructions.
existing.selection_notes: A specialized OAS and UDD committee selects the recipients. Elements considered in awarding the scholarships are geographic distribution of the candidates, the applicant's profile including education and project outline and recommendation, the applicant's potential impact on completion of the course, and gender distribution. A selection committee pre-selects participants on that profile; pre-selected participants may be interviewed in English. Results are published at www.oas.org/scholarships by February 2027, and unsuccessful applicants are not contacted.
existing.best_fit: Young professionals from OAS Member States other than Chile who have a business management background, a strong interest in innovation and entrepreneurship, and can commit about 4.5 hours a week in English to a fully online course.
existing.notes: This is a fee-reduction award, not a living stipend: the scholarship covers USD 3,400 of a USD 3,800 course fee and the recipient must find USD 400 plus study materials, equipment and internet access themselves. No living cost, travel or health insurance funding is published, so applicants must not budget this as full funding. Not eligible: current OAS scholarship recipients, GS/OAS staff and their immediate family, GS/OAS consultants, and permanent OAS staff and their immediate family. The recipient may decline the scholarship before the program start date without financial penalty, but declining after that date without proof of force majeure may require repayment of all funds awarded. The GS/OAS reserves the right to cancel this scholarship announcement at any time during the process.
existing.application_period: Applications accepted through the OAS online application link until 31 January 2027; results published at www.oas.org/scholarships by February 2027; course runs 16 March to 22 June 2027.

scholarships.title: Programa de Becas de Cooperacion Sur-Sur - Republica de Chile 2027 (AGCID)
scholarships.official_source: Agencia Chilena de Cooperacion Internacional para el Desarrollo (AGCID), Government of Chile

eligibility: National of one of the countries listed in the call: Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Cuba, Ecuador, Mexico, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras, Panama, Dominican Republic and the CARICOM member states
Age over 20 and under 65 at the closing date of the call
Professional undergraduate degree from a recognised higher-education institution
Cumulative undergraduate GPA of at least 4.0/5.0 evidenced by an official transcript
Unconditional admission letter from the Chilean institution for a master's programme listed in Anexo 1
Resident in their country of origin at the time of application
Not in arrears with ICETEX credit lines or administered funds (checked in ICETEX systems)
Priority given to public officials and to academic, teaching or research staff of recognised higher-education institutions

Applicants in public entities, ministries, public services, state institutions or companies, as well as staff of recognised higher-education institutions, may apply; professionals linked to civil-society organisations may also apply if they meet the requirements
existing.eligibility_summary: Nationals of Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Cuba, Ecuador, Mexico, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras, Panama, the Dominican Republic and CARICOM member states who hold a professional undergraduate degree, have a cumulative GPA of at least 4.0/5.0, are aged over 20 and under 65 at the closing date, and already hold unconditional admission to an accredited Chilean master's programme listed in Anexo 1 of the call. Applicants must be resident in their country of origin and must return there after the programme.
benefits: Full tuition, matricula and titulation costs at an accredited Chilean institution
CLP 600,000 monthly maintenance stipend for in-person or hybrid programmes with presence in Chile
Life, health and accident insurance for in-country study
Priority weighting for master's programmes in areas designated strategic by the Government of Chile
coverage: 100% of matricula, arancel (tuition) and graduation costs charged by the Chilean higher-education institution, for up to four academic semesters or six quarters
Monthly maintenance allowance of CLP 600,000 for up to 24 months, only for programmes delivered in person or hybrid with physical presence in Chile
Life, health and accident insurance for the duration of the scholarship, only for scholars studying in Chile
One-time allocation of CLP 90,000 for textbooks and study materials in the first academic term, only for programmes delivered in Chile
One-time allocation of CLP 300,000 to support thesis or final-degree project costs, subject to AGCID academic conditions
requirements: Secure unconditional admission to a Chilean master's programme listed in Anexo 1 of the call, at the applicant's own cost
Submit the official AGCID ANEXO 4 scholarship application form, typed on a computer and signed, using the unmodified official layout
Submit the ANEXO 5 health declaration and pre-existing conditions statement signed by a licensed physician
Submit the ANEXO 4 form and the AGCID master's-programme-and-scholar information format, both mandatory, in their official layout
Upload all documents as legible PDFs in Spanish; illegible, password-protected or non-Spanish documents are discarded
Reach a minimum of 55 base points in the preselection scoring to be considered at all
Remain exclusively dedicated to the funded study programme and comply with AGCID academic and administrative rules
documents: ANEXO 4 - Formulario de Solicitud de Beca AGCID, completed on computer and signed
Carta de aceptacion definitiva del programa de magisteria, on university letterhead, stating unconditional acceptance, delivery mode, start and end dates, and the matricula and annual arancel values
ANEXO 5 - Declaracion de Salud y Enfermedades Preexistentes, signed by a licensed physician
Titulo universitario de pregrado, digital copy, with official Spanish translation if issued abroad
Certificado de notas de pregrado showing the weighted cumulative average, issued and signed by the institution; foreign transcripts must state the grading scale from 1 to 5

Certificados de experiencia profesional laboral relacionada, naming the employer, dates of service and functions; the current-employment certificate must be no more than 30 calendar days old at the closing date

Socioeconomic evidence: a copy of a domestic public-utility bill (electricity, gas or water) issued within the last 60 working days showing estrato and address, and where SISBEN IV applies a screenshot or certificate of the SISBEN IV category updated for 2025
Hoja de vida (CV) emphasising academic training and professional experience
Carta de motivacion in Spanish, dated and signed, of about one to two pages and at least 500 words
Propuesta preliminar de tesis, about one page
Una carta de referencia academica, dated and signed; letters from relatives are not accepted
Carta de patrocinio de la entidad empleadora, where the applicant is employed
AGCID information format for the master's programme and the scholarship holder
Legible copy of the national identity card on both sides; a valid passport is the selected scholar's own responsibility for the whole programme
application_method: Apply through the ICETEX postulation platform as focal point for Colombia; applications sent directly to AGCID are not considered
Upload every required document as a legible Spanish PDF in the platform
Preselection by the Comision Nacional de Becas on 26 October 2026
ICETEX forwards its ranked preselected list to AGCID, whose Selection Committee makes the final, definitive and unappealable decision
Definitive results communicated from the second half of November 2026 via the AGCID results page
The award is formalised by signing the AGCID scholarship acceptance document (ANEXO 2)
existing.selection_notes: Preselection is scored out of 100 base points: related professional experience 40% (more than 85 months 40 pts; 61-84 months 35 pts; 37-60 months 30 pts; 12-36 months 25 pts); academic average 40% (4.6-5.0 gives 40 pts; 4.3-4.5 gives 30 pts; 4.0-4.2 gives 20 pts); socioeconomic factor 20% (SISBEN IV categories A1-B7 give 20 pts, C1-C18 18 pts, D1-D3 16 pts, D4-D21 14 pts; where no SISBEN IV is available, estratos 1-2 give 12 pts, estratos 3-4 10 pts, estratos 5-6 8 pts). Up to 10 non-cumulative bonus points are available for working as a public official or as academic, teaching or research staff at a recognised higher-education institution; for a master's in a Chilean-government priority area; for membership of an ethnic community recognised by the Ministry of the Interior; for being certified a victim of the armed conflict through the RUV; and for having been a beneficiary of an ICETEX credit or administered fund. A minimum of 55 base points is required. Tiebreakers in order: highest academic average, then preference for women as recorded on the identity card, then earliest completed submission.
existing.best_fit: Mid-career professionals from Latin America and the Caribbean who already hold unconditional admission to an accredited Chilean master's programme and have a strong academic record, limited means, or membership of a priority group.
existing.notes: Admission and funding are separate steps: the applicant must already hold an unconditional acceptance letter from a Chilean institution for a programme listed in Anexo 1, and pays all admission-related costs, before the scholarship can be applied for. Applications for programmes not in Anexo 1 are not considered. AGCID scholarships are incompatible with any other AGCID scholarship for study in Chile, and a spouse who holds an AGCID scholarship in the same call is also excluded. Scholars must return to their country of origin after the programme in order to apply and replicate what they have learned, which is stated as a condition of the award.
existing.duration: Up to 24 months (maximum four academic semesters or six quarters), aligned to the official duration of the chosen master's programme
existing.application_period: 12 August 2026 to 9 October 2026, 13:00 (Colombian focal-point window); programmes start between 1 March and 30 September 2027
existing.deadline_display: 9 October 2026, 1:00 p.m. Colombia time (ICETEX channel deadline for the Colombian focal point)
